articles.title: Meliá Chiang Mai Celebrates ‘The Sweet Life’ With Spanish-Inspired Afternoon Tea
articles.titleKo: Meliá Chiang Mai Celebrates ‘The Sweet Life’ With Spanish-Inspired Afternoon Tea
articles.originalSummary: From chorizo-filled brioche buns to Spain’s famed caramelised custard dessert, Meliá Chiang Mai’s new La Vida Dulce Afternoon Tea is a tribute to the sweeter side of life, accompanied by sweeping views of the city and famed Doi Suthep Temple on the mountaintop to the west. Meaning “the sweet life” in Spanish, La Vida Dulce Afternoon Tea for two references Meliá’s Spanish origins and is served daily at the hotel’s signature Mai Restaurant & Bar on the 21st floor until January 31, 2027. Savoury delights include Spanish ham croquettes, chorizo and cheese brioche buns known as Bollos Preñaos , crabmeat and avocado timbales, and Manchego cheese scones with strawberry jam and cream. Sweet treats range from white chocolate cake and Crema Catalana , Spain’s traditional custard dessert, to refreshing lemon ice popsicles. The afternoon tea is accompanied by Meliá Chiang Mai’s popular mocktail Meliá Blossom, a sublime concoction of lychee juice, lime juice, cherry blossom syrup and grenadine, finished with a coral vine flower garnish. Inclusive of a selection of fine teas or coffee, afternoon tea is presented in a vintage tea cabinet crafted at Baan Tawai, providing a glimpse into the region’s rich heritage of woodcraft. Situated in Chiang Mai’s Hang Dong District, Baan Tawai is a community renowned for its wood sculptures, bustling markets and skilled wood carvers whose craftsmanship has been handed down through the generations. An intimate fine-dining restaurant serving contemporary Northern Thai dishes accompanied by spectacular vistas, Mai Restaurant and Bar is a visual marvel. Guests enter the venue under an arch that pays homage to a nearby temple. In a salute to Chiang Mai’s Bo Sang Umbrella Village, large installations of illuminated umbrella ribs cling to the ceiling. Various artworks depicting umbrella canopies, including those crafted from antique Chiang Mai textiles, adorn the walls. Priced at THB 999 (USD 30) net for a set inclusive of two glasses of Meliá Blossom and a choice of tea or coffee, La Vida Dulce Afternoon Tea is served from 2pm to 5pm daily. A second option, priced at THB 1,599 (USD 48) net per set, includes two glasses of sparkling wine and a choice of tea or coffee. For more information and reservations, please contact 052 090 603 or email mairestaurant@meliachiangmai.com Prices are inclusive of 10% service charge and 7% government tax. Terms and conditions apply.

articles.title: American Express and IDA Mark Five Years of Backing International Small Restaurants As 2026 UK Applications Open
articles.titleKo: American Express and IDA Mark Five Years of Backing International Small Restaurants As 2026 UK Applications Open
articles.originalSummary: Independent restaurants in London and Manchester can now apply for a share of £210,000 in grant funding, as American Express and the International Downtown Association Foundation (IDA) today launched this year’s Backing International Small Restaurants grants programme, open for applications through November 16, 2026. Celebrating its fifth anniversary globally and in the UK, the programme plans to award more than £1.1 million to support over 100 independent restaurants across nine countries and expands to Italy for the first time. The programme supports small, independent restaurants as they grow, recover and support their local communities, including investments that help strengthen their operations and long-term resilience. Backing International Small Restaurants plans to award £10,500 grants to 20 independent restaurants across London and Manchester through the International Downtown Association Foundation (IDA), in partnership with the Association of Town & City Management (ATCM) in the UK. Dan Edelman, UK General Manager of Merchant Services at American Express , said: “Independent restaurants play an important role in bringing communities together, and we’re proud to have backed them through this programme for five years in the UK. By helping restaurant owners invest in their businesses and long-term growth, we hope to create an impact that extends beyond their doors to the communities they serve.” Among the programme’s previous UK recipients is Grounded, a community cafe in Manchester. Natalie Lobel, Co-Founder of Grounded, reflects on the effects of the grant: “The funding from Backing International Small Restaurants has had a lasting impact on Grounded. By helping us improve our outdoor space, we’ve been able to increase capacity, welcome more customers throughout the year and build a stronger, business for the long-term. This grant allowed us to continue investing in our community and provide healthy and affordable food.” Globally, Backing International Small Restaurants grants programme has grown from five cities in five countries in 2022 to 15 cities across nine countries in 2026. Over the past four years, more than £2.4 million has been awarded to over 230 restaurants worldwide. Supporting the UK’s independent restaurants Highlighting the important role independent restaurants play in the UK’s hospitality sector and local communities, Allen Simpson, Chief Executive of UKHospitality , said: “Independent restaurants are a significant part of what make our high streets, towns and cities thriving hubs of activity. With many independents navigating financial pressures, the Backing International Small Restaurants grant programme is incredibly valuable in helping businesses make essential maintenance, invest in their venue or offer and, crucially, provide the sector with some much-needed support.” David Downey, Executive Director, IDA Foundation , said : “As we celebrate five years of Backing International Small Restaurants, we’re proud of the programme’s growth and impact on independent restaurants around the world. We continue to be inspired by our grantees, whose passion and leadership help make neighbourhoods vibrant and connected. With the ongoing support of American Express, we’re helping strengthen local economies and communities across the globe.” Applications for the 2026 Backing International Small Restaurants programme close on 16 November 2026 . Independent restaurant owners in London and Manchester can find out more and apply at downtown.org/foundation.

articles.title: DoorDash Announces Deal to Acquire Instacart for $17 Billion
articles.titleKo: DoorDash Announces Deal to Acquire Instacart for $17 Billion
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The value of $65 per Instacart share represents a 26 percent premium to Instacart's closing price on October 22. DoorDash, Inc. and Maplebear Inc. (d.b.a. Instacart) announced a definitive agreement under which DoorDash will acquire Instacart for a total value of $65 for each Instacart share, or an equity value of approximately $17 billion. The aggregate transaction consideration will be at least 75 percent cash, with Instacart stockholders able to elect cash, DoorDash stock, or a combination of both, subject to proration so that DoorDash stock does not exceed 25 percent of the aggregate consideration. Instacart’s board of directors has unanimously approved the agreement. DoorDash and Instacart share a mission to help local businesses succeed. Families turn to Instacart for the big weekly shop and to DoorDash for meals and nearly anything else they need from their neighborhood in under an hour. The combined company will offer grocers and retailers of every size DoorDash’s delivery network and Instacart’s grocery and fulfillment technology, in both apps and on stores’ own websites, along with the advertising and AI tools each company has built. On either app, customers pick a store in their own community, and the store makes the sale. Consumers will have more stores to choose from, more savings opportunities when they choose to shop with a local business, and faster delivery options, while Dashers and Shoppers will have more ways to earn, the company said. Most grocery shopping still happens in stores, but more people are buying groceries and everyday goods online, it added. “They expect fast, affordable delivery and an easy way to order,” a release stated. “The biggest online retailers and grocers are racing ahead, building their own delivery fleets, warehouses, membership programs, and AI shopping assistants. A grocer or retailer running on thin margins cannot build all of that alone, and with AI, the playing field risks being tilted even further away from local commerce.” The release continued: “DoorDash and Instacart believe that communities benefit when Main Street competes, and they build the tools that empower local businesses. Together, they could help local stores grow online. More grocers could deploy Instacart’s technology to run their own websites and retail media networks, bringing them more sales and advertising revenue. Brands would gain a scaled alternative for reaching customers online. Grocers could add capacity for online orders through DoorDash’s DashMart Fulfillment Services and offer faster, more accurate, and more affordable delivery.” “Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online. Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you’d choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts,” said Tony Xu, co-founder and CEO of DoorDash, in a statement. “Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery. It’s still early innings, but we know that when more people shop local, more dollars stay local.” “Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more,” noted Chris Rogers, CEO of Instacart. “When our purpose-built grocery technology and trusted retailer and brand relationships are combined with DoorDash’s global consumer reach and logistics capabilities, we can create new opportunities for our retail and brand partners, offer an even better experience for customers and shoppers, and deliver compelling value for our shareholders. articles.title: Raffles Grand Hotel d’Angkor Presents ‘The Grand Table’ Culinary Weekend
articles.titleKo: Raffles Grand Hotel d’Angkor Presents ‘The Grand Table’ Culinary Weekend
articles.originalSummary: Exclusive dining events in Siem Reap bring together four of Cambodia’s most celebrated chefs and one of the city’s standout bartenders Raffles Grand Hotel d’Angkor will host ‘The Grand Table’, an exclusive culinary weekend uniting four of Cambodia’s most celebrated chefs and one of Siem Reap’s standout bartenders from Nov. 6-8. The three-day event features Executive Chef Memo Hernandez and Chef Dorn Doeurt of Raffles Grand Hotel d’Angkor, Executive Chef David Eldridge of Raffles Hotel Le Royal, Chef Aude Moulard of Taties Phnom Penh, and bartender Amine Birdouz of Calao Bar. Across a series of special dining and drinking experiences, the chefs and bartender bring together their distinctive heritage, creativity and culinary philosophy, creating a celebration of culture, craftsmanship and flavour where refined elegance meets technical precision. “The Grand Table is a celebration of Cambodia’s extraordinary culinary talent and the spirit of generosity that defines Raffles. By bringing these exceptional chefs and bartender together under one roof, we invite our guests to experience the stories, heritage and craftsmanship that make dining and nightlife in Cambodia so memorable,” said Joseph Colina, General Manager of Raffles Grand Hotel d’Angkor. The weekend opens with an exclusive cocktail evening on Nov. 6 from 6 p.m. onward, as Calao Bar takes over the legendary Elephant Bar at Raffles Grand Hotel d’Angkor for one night only. Guests can enjoy a curated selection of signature cocktails from one of Cambodia’s most exciting bar teams while meeting the visiting chefs and fellow epicureans in classic Raffles style. An evening of culinary artistry and storytelling follows on Nov. 7, when the four chefs each present a signature course inspired by their culture, memories and culinary roots at Raffles Marquee. Each dish draws on the chef’s personal history and tradition, offering guests a deeper connection to the stories behind the food. The 5-course meal, accompanied by pre-dinner cocktails, is priced at $90++ per person, starting at 6:30 p.m for drinks (dining from 7 p.m.). The weekend concludes on the morning of Nov. 8 as the chefs reimagine Siem Reap’s most iconic Champagne Brunch at Café d’Angkor. Guests will enjoy a collection of signature dishes that bring fresh creativity and craftsmanship to the city’s favourite weekend tradition. The brunch is priced at $60++ per person. During their stay in Siem Reap, the chefs will also visit hospitality schools including Paul Dubrule and Sala Baï to share their professional journeys and insights with the next generation of hospitality talent. “I’m excited to be back at my culinary school,” said Chef Dorn Doeurt, an alumnus of Paul Dubrule. “It’s a special opportunity to reconnect with the place that shaped me and to share what I’ve learned with the students who are just starting their own journeys.” “Beyond the culinary offers of the weekend itself, I am passionate about continuing to support the local community by creating opportunities such as this for students to learn, grow, and gain valuable industry exposure,” added Executive Chef Memo Hernandez. For more information on ‘The Grand Table’ at Raffles Grand Hotel d’Angkor, please call +855 23 982 598 or visit www.raffles.com/siem-reap/

articles.title: PF indicia Vorcaro e mais 14 investigados no caso Master
articles.titleKo: PF indicia Vorcaro e mais 14 investigados no caso Master
articles.originalSummary: A Polícia Federal (PF) indiciou nesta quarta-feira, 28, o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro e mais 14 investigados pelas fraudes financeiras no Banco Regional de Brasília (BRB). As irregularidades foram investigadas na primeira fase da Operação Compliance Zero. De acordo com relatório de indiciamentos, Vorcaro teve “participação pessoal, reiterada e diretiva” nas operações com carteiras de créditos irregulares do Banco Master que causam prejuízos ao BRB. “Na condição de controlador do Banco Master, Vorcaro ocupava o centro decisório da estrutura examinada e era o principal beneficiário econômico das operações destinadas à obtenção de liquidez para a instituição”, concluiu a PF. Vorcaro foi preso em março deste ano e está custodiado no presídio da Papudinha, no Distrito Federal. Além de Vorcaro, também estão na lista de indiciados o ex-presidente do BRB Paulo Henrique Costa e Augusto Lima, ex-sócio do Master. Todos os investigados foram acusados dos crimes de gestão fraudulenta de instituição financeira, organização criminosa e lavagem de dinheiro. Prejuízo De acordo com os investigadores da PF, o prejuízo já apurado é de aproximadamente R$ 2,7 bilhões. Parte das perdas foram provocadas por carteiras de créditos inexistentes, que estavam em nome da Tirreno, empresa de fachada operada pelo Master, e que fez transações com o BRB. “Há, portanto, aproximadamente R$ 2,7 bilhões em perdas já formalizadas e reconhecidas, não se tratando de estimativa abstrata ou de risco meramente eventual”, afirmou a PF. Após concluir a primeira parte da Operação Compliance Zero, os investigadores enviaram o relatório de indiciamentos à Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) e solicitaram ao Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) prorrogação das investigações por mais 60 dias. O prazo será utilizado para conclusão dos exames periciais que estão pendentes e apresentação de um relatório complementar de investigação. Com informações de Agência Brasil. Imagem: Secretaria de Administração Penitenciária de SP O post PF indicia Vorcaro e mais 14 investigados no caso Master apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Palladino Group has appointed John Tesar corporate executive chef, overseeing Palladino’s Steak & Seafood at Grand Central Terminal in New York and its new Dallas location in Preston Hollow. Tesar joins restaurateur Joseph Palladino, whose restaurant background includes Nick & Sam’s. The two have known each other for approximately two decades, and Palladino previously discussed a partnership with Tesar before the timing aligned. Under Tesar, Palladino’s is expanding its seafood and Italian offerings. Additions include tableside Dover sole with brown butter and capers, along with flat iron, skirt, and baseball steaks. The dishes join the restaurant’s existing prime beef and sushi selections. Tesar began his career at Club Pierre in Westhampton, New York, before opening 13 Barrow Street and working at Manhattan restaurants including 44 & X, Vine, and the Supper Club. His career later took him to Las Vegas and Dallas, where he opened Spoon and Knife. His work at Knife & Spoon earned Michelin stars in 2022 and 2023. Tesar is also a five-time James Beard Award semifinalist for Best Chef Southwest and competed on two seasons of Bravo’s Top Chef . Tesar divides his time between Palladino’s Grand Central Terminal restaurant and its Dallas location at 5959 Royal Lane. More information is available at palladinos.com. In his new role, Chef Rivera will lead culinary direction across The Lounge, banquet services, in-room dining, weddings, and special events. “This is an exciting moment for Conrad Indianapolis, and I’m honored to lead the culinary team into its next chapter,” said Chef Rivera. “My focus is on delivering exceptional, ingredient-driven dining experiences that honor the hotel’s luxury heritage while introducing thoughtful, contemporary approaches across every touchpoint of our food and beverage program.” With a career rooted in luxury hospitality, Chef Rivera brings more than 15 years of culinary experience to his role from some of the industry’s most respected hotels, resorts and restaurant concepts. He joins Conrad Indianapolis from Conrad Orlando , where he served as Chef de Cuisine and helped lead one of the resort’s premier high-volume dining operations. His hospitality background also includes culinary leadership roles at luxury resorts and restaurant concepts across Florida and Puerto Rico. “We are thrilled to welcome Chef Kenneth Rivera to the Conrad Indianapolis family,” said Ryan Fitzgerald, general manager, Conrad Indianapolis. “His track record of excellence in luxury resorts and high-volume operations brings invaluable expertise to our team as we continue to refresh our spaces and elevate every touchpoint of our guest experience.” Chef Rivera’s connection to food began early in life in his family’s restaurant, shaping a culinary philosophy centered on fresh ingredients, disciplined technique, and respect for origin. At Conrad Indianapolis, he brings that foundation to a culinary program focused on creating dining experiences that are both refined and approachable. For more information, to make a reservation at The Lounge or to book a stay, please visit www.conradindianapolis.com. Read more about Conrad Hotels & Resorts at stories.hilton.com/conradhotels. Together they relaunched Annabel’s and transformed The Roof Gardens in Kensington into one of London’s leading private members’ clubs. “After watching the success of our second season, we knew we could do so much more,” said Frankie and Luis. “Sunset Harbour has embraced us, and we want to give the neighborhood a place they can return to throughout the day, whether that’s a weekday breakfast, a long weekend brunch or a celebratory dinner. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Meridian, the acclaimed restaurant located at The Village Dallas, is welcoming the cooler months with a new fall/winter menu from Executive Chef Eduardo Osorio. Rooted in the restaurant’s signature live-fire cooking style, the seasonal menu introduces an array of new dishes and fresh takes on guest favorites, showcasing autumn produce, rich flavors and thoughtfully sourced ingredients. Blending modern American cuisine with Italian and Mediterranean influences, Meridian’s latest offerings celebrate the season through comforting, craveable dishes that balance familiar flavors with inventive culinary techniques. From vibrant seasonal vegetables and handmade pastas to hearth-fired seafood and premium cuts of beef, the new menu reflects Chef Osorio’s commitment to letting quality ingredients shine. A new addition to Meridian’s signature “One-Hitters” selection is the Caviar with ham hock egg custard, sunchoke foam and croutons. The Autumn Chicory Salad brings together castelfranco, endive and frisée with fire-roasted beets, goat cheese, shallot crumble and rosé vinaigrette, while the Honeynut Squash offers a comforting combination of stracciatella, brown butter and toasted pepitas and golden raisins. For heartier fare, guests can enjoy the new Braised Short Rib Cappelletti, featuring pecorino, ricotta, parsnip, ricotta, parmesan foam, truffled Madeira jus and pickled onions. Meridian’s signature hearth remains at the center of the dining experience, with new dishes and seasonal accompaniments highlighting the depth of flavor achieved through live-fire cooking. The Coal-Roasted Dorade, designed for sharing, is served with red kuri-curry, turnips, coconut basmati rice, coriander, fennel and garden herbs. Returning favorites have also received seasonal updates, including the Texas Wagyu Chef’s Cut with chanterelles, pickled black trumpet mushrooms, leeks and au poivre; the 35-Day Dry-Aged Ribeye with escargot and tarragon butter and bordelaise; and the Wood-Fired Half Chicken with cannellini beans, Swiss chard, pearl onions, guindilla peppers and chicken jus. The new seasonal accompaniment is the Hearth-Grilled Sunchokes, served with sunchoke purée, warm spices, toasted cashews and brown butter vinaigrette. The seasonal menu also reflects Meridian’s ongoing commitment to working with farms and purveyors that share its dedication to quality ingredients. The restaurant is proud to partner with Millbrook Mushrooms (Rockwall, TX), Southern Sunny Acres (Winona, TX), Rae Lili Farms (Cooper, TX) and Rosewood Wagyu (Dallas, TX), whose products help inspire the restaurant’s ingredient-driven approach and evolving seasonal offerings. Meridian’s fall/winter menu is now available. To make a reservation go to https://www.opentable.com/r/meridian-dallas. articles.title: Fed mantém juros entre 3,75% e 4% ao ano, com dois votos por alta
articles.titleKo: Fed mantém juros entre 3,75% e 4% ao ano, com dois votos por alta
articles.originalSummary: O Federal Reserve (Fed), banco central dos Estados Unidos, manteve a taxa básica de juros na faixa entre 3,75% e 4% ao ano. A decisão foi aprovada por 10 votos a 2 pelo Comitê Federal de Mercado Aberto ( FOMC ), que destacou a resiliência dos gastos domésticos e o ritmo forte da atividade econômica, mas ressaltou que a inflação continua elevada. Na avaliação do Comitê, a economia americana segue em expansão acelerada, com crescimento da produtividade e investimentos de capital robustos. A geração de empregos acompanhou o crescimento da força de trabalho, enquanto a taxa de desemprego apresentou pouca variação. Apesar desses indicadores, o Fed afirmou que precisa reunir mais informações para definir os próximos passos da política monetária e garantir que a inflação retorne à meta de 2%. As diretoras Lisa D. Cook e Beth M. Hammack votaram contra a manutenção da taxa e defenderam uma elevação de 0,25 ponto percentual nesta reunião. Com isso, a decisão de manter os juros foi aprovada sem unanimidade. O Comitê também reiterou a política de manter um nível amplo de reservas no sistema bancário. articles.title: Coca-Cola Femsa cresce 3,9% em volume no Brasil, mas banco prevê estagnação em 2027
articles.titleKo: Coca-Cola Femsa cresce 3,9% em volume no Brasil, mas banco prevê estagnação em 2027
articles.originalSummary: A Coca-Cola Femsa reportou ao mercado crescimento de 3,9% no volume de bebidas comercializadas no Brasil no terceiro trimestre de 2026 , na comparação com o mesmo período do ano passado. O resultado contribuiu para o avanço das operações da companhia na América do Sul, mas não afastou as preocupações do BTG Pactual com o desempenho do mercado brasileiro em 2027. Em relatório divulgado nesta quarta-feira, 28, o banco projeta estabilidade dos volumes vendidos no País no próximo ano, em um cenário de custo elevado de capital e menor previsibilidade para o consumo. A avaliação acompanha a divulgação dos resultados trimestrais da Coca-Cola Femsa, maior engarrafadora de produtos Coca-Cola do mundo em volume de vendas. Globalmente, a companhia registrou receita de 79,72 bilhões de pesos mexicanos, crescimento de 10,9% em relação ao terceiro trimestre de 2025. Desconsiderando os efeitos cambiais, o avanço foi de 11,3%. O volume consolidado de bebidas comercializadas alcançou 1,09 bilhão de caixas unitárias, alta de 5,3%. Além do Brasil, contribuíram para esse desempenho o México, com crescimento de 4,2% em volume, a Colômbia, com 15,9%, e a América Central, com avanços nas diferentes operações. Na divisão da América do Sul, que reúne Brasil, Argentina, Colômbia e Uruguai, a receita totalizou 33,74 bilhões de pesos mexicanos, crescimento de 14,7%. O volume vendido aumentou 6%, para 448,3 milhões de caixas unitárias. Somente o Brasil respondeu por 290 milhões de caixas unitárias, ante 279,2 milhões no terceiro trimestre de 2025. Lucro líquido avança 5,5% e Ebitda cresce 16,2% O lucro líquido consolidado atribuível aos acionistas da Coca-Cola Femsa alcançou 6,22 bilhões de pesos mexicanos no terceiro trimestre, crescimento de 5,5% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado. A evolução foi sustentada principalmente pelo aumento do resultado operacional, parcialmente compensado por maiores despesas financeiras e impostos. O Ebitda ajustado divulgado pela companhia somou 16,79 bilhões de pesos mexicanos, avanço de 16,2%. Já o lucro operacional atingiu 11,87 bilhões de pesos mexicanos, crescimento de 15,4%, com margem de 14,9%, aumento de 0,6 ponto percentual. Parte desse desempenho foi favorecida pelo reconhecimento de um ganho não recorrente de 1,055 bilhão de pesos mexicanos, líquido de despesas, relacionado a indenizações de seguros no Brasil. Excluindo efeitos extraordinários, o BTG estima crescimento de 10,6% no Ebitda ajustado em sua análise comparável, com ligeira contração da margem consolidada. Na América do Sul, o Ebitda ajustado divulgado pela companhia cresceu 39,7%, para 7,22 bilhões de pesos mexicanos. O lucro operacional da divisão avançou 51,2%, beneficiado pelo ganho extraordinário, pela maior escala das operações e por iniciativas de eficiência. A Coca-Cola Femsa encerrou setembro com dívida líquida de 39,89 bilhões de pesos mexicanos, considerando os efeitos de instrumentos de proteção financeira. O montante representa uma redução de 24,5% em relação aos 52,85 bilhões registrados em dezembro de 2025. A relação entre dívida líquida e Ebitda ajustado recuou de 0,89 para 0,63 vez. BTG vê risco para volumes no Brasil em 2027 Apesar dos resultados favoráveis, o BTG Pactual reduziu sua recomendação para as ações da Coca-Cola Femsa de compra para neutra. A decisão considera a valorização de aproximadamente 30% dos papéis em 2026, o custo de capital mais elevado no Brasil e a visibilidade limitada sobre a evolução dos volumes comercializados em 2027. O banco estima que as vendas em volume da companhia permaneçam estáveis no mercado brasileiro no próximo ano, enquanto no México a projeção é de crescimento de 2%. Os analistas destacam que a Coca-Cola Femsa mantém uma posição competitiva sólida e oportunidades de expansão em diferentes mercados. articles.title: Grupo Pereira abre 100 vagas para pessoas em processo de ressocialização
articles.titleKo: Grupo Pereira abre 100 vagas para pessoas em processo de ressocialização
articles.originalSummary: O Grupo Pereira está com 100 vagas abertas para o restaurante Trudy’s por meio do projeto Reeducandos, iniciativa que conecta pessoas em processo de ressocialização ao mercado formal de trabalho. Criado em 2014, o programa já beneficiou mais de 800 pessoas, incluindo mais de 100 no Rio Grande do Sul, e atualmente conta com 260 participantes ativos em diferentes operações da companhia. Das oportunidades disponíveis, 36 são para auxiliar de cozinha no Distrito Federal, em Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul e no Rio Grande do Sul. Em Canoas (RS), duas participantes do programa já trabalham no restaurante Trudy’s. A iniciativa também está presente nas bandeiras Fort Atacadista e Comper. O projeto busca ampliar as oportunidades de trabalho e renda para pessoas em processo de ressocialização, contribuindo para a reinserção social e a redução da reincidência criminal. Os participantes atuam em diferentes áreas do Grupo Pereira, como logística, manutenção, apoio operacional, televendas e centros de distribuição. A seleção é realizada em parceria com as secretarias de administração penitenciária locais. Os trabalhadores recebem remuneração, alimentação, transporte e uniformes, além de participar de atividades de capacitação sobre ressocialização, comportamento no ambiente de trabalho e desenvolvimento profissional. O programa também permite aos participantes remir parte da pena pelo trabalho, conforme a legislação aplicável: a cada três dias trabalhados, é possível reduzir um dia de condenação. Trabalho como ferramenta de ressocialização Para Kariny Santos, coordenadora nacional de Gente e Gestão do Grupo Pereira, a oferta de trabalho formal contribui para devolver autonomia às pessoas atendidas e ampliar as possibilidades de reinserção social. A iniciativa ocorre em um contexto de desafios para a inclusão profissional dessa população. Dados citados pela Secretaria Nacional de Políticas Penais indicam que menos de 30% das pessoas privadas de liberdade têm acesso a atividades laborais, enquanto o preconceito e a falta de oportunidades dificultam a entrada no mercado de trabalho. “Participar deste projeto, realizando a integração, conscientizando as lideranças e proporcionando novas oportunidades, é gratificante pessoal e profissionalmente. Ver pessoas recomeçando suas trajetórias com mais confiança e dignidade, reforça que nosso maior investimento sempre será nas pessoas. É motivo de muito orgulho saber que estamos impulsionando esse movimento de impacto social no mercado brasileiro, contribuindo com a quebra do estigma na hora da contratação definitiva”, reflete Kariny. articles.title: Electrolux conecta instaladores à fábrica e amplia suporte técnico para ar-condicionado
articles.titleKo: Electrolux conecta instaladores à fábrica e amplia suporte técnico para ar-condicionado
articles.originalSummary: A Electrolux reforça os canais de suporte técnico para instaladores de ar-condicionado por meio da plataforma Electrolux Instala, que conecta profissionais em campo à equipe de engenharia e suporte da fábrica em tempo real. O atendimento é feito por telefone 0800 e WhatsApp e busca esclarecer dúvidas durante a execução dos serviços , especialmente com a proximidade da temporada de calor extremo. A iniciativa considera que mais de 80% dos problemas operacionais em aparelhos de ar-condicionado decorrem de falhas de instalação, e não de defeitos de fabricação. A qualidade do serviço também influencia a escolha do consumidor: pesquisas da marca indicam que mais de 40% das decisões por uma marca de ar-condicionado são influenciadas pela recomendação do instalador. “O ar-condicionado é uma categoria altamente dependente de mão de obra qualificada e, ao abrirmos as portas da fábrica para ouvir as críticas, dúvidas e sugestões desses profissionais, elevamos o padrão de entrega em toda a jornada. Nosso objetivo com os canais e programas de capacitação é oferecer o respaldo técnico necessário para que o instalador trabalhe com confiança e o consumidor desfrute do máximo desempenho do seu produto”, destaca Elizeu Silva, supervisor de Treinamentos do Electrolux Group. O Electrolux Instala reúne mais de 20 mil profissionais cadastrados e oferece capacitação gratuita para iniciantes e especialistas. Os conteúdos abrangem técnicas de instalação e manutenção, gestão de pequenos negócios, finanças, legislação e normas técnicas, como o Plano de Manutenção, Operação e Controle (PMOC). Produtos e serviços de suporte A experiência dos profissionais também orientou o desenvolvimento da linha Max Comfort, lançada pela Electrolux na categoria de ar-condicionado. O modelo conta com suportes redesenhados e mecanismos que permitem ajustar a angulação do aparelho e realizar procedimentos de manutenção sem removê-lo da parede. A empresa também oferece cinco anos de garantia total para o produto e dez anos para o compressor, desde que a instalação siga as instruções do manual técnico. Segundo a companhia, a garantia não exige credenciamento exclusivo nem vínculo restritivo com a marca. Para os consumidores, o suporte inclui o Electrolux Cuida, site que reúne agendamento de serviços, benefícios e conteúdos. A plataforma permite solicitar a instalação de aparelhos e, para ampliar a disponibilidade do atendimento, conecta clientes a profissionais capacitados cadastrados no Electrolux Instala. Academy Award-nominee, Taraji P. Henson, is bringing a little extra sparkle to P.F. Chang’s. The leading Pan-Asian restaurant brand debuted a newly redesigned wine list, featuring Seven Daughters Moscato, now available by the glass and by the bottle, from the wine brand for which Henson serves as Strategic Advisor and Creative Collaborator. In addition, guests can also enjoy a new weekday Happy Hour, featuring the much-anticipated $15 Sushi & Sip pairing, along with several of this year’s most popular limited-time dishes, which now have a permanent home on the main menu. The new wine list is organized by flavor profile rather than varietal, from Sparkling & Refreshing to Full & Bold, with pairing suggestions now appearing beside select dishes throughout the menu. Seven Daughters Moscato is featured as the suggested pairing for P.F. Chang’s Dynamite Shrimp, tempura-battered and tossed in a sriracha aioli. Other new additions include Gratien Meyer Crémant de Loire Brut Rosé, Belle Glos “Las Alturas” Pinot Noir, Stags’ Leap “Aveta” Sauvignon Blanc, Penfolds Max’s Shiraz and DAOU Cabernet Sauvignon. Separate from the new wine list, P.F. Chang’s new Happy Hour runs Monday through Friday from 3 to 6 p.m. in the bar and on the patio at participating locations where permitted by applicable law, featuring $6 select beer and wine, $9 cocktails, $12 full-size appetizers and the new $15 Sushi & Sip offering. The most awaited addition, Sushi & Sip pairs a Spicy Tuna or California Roll with Sapporo or Joto One “Graffiti Cup” Sake, a single-serve sake whose cup was designed by Japanese graffiti artist, Shiro. Fan favorite Japanese Wok-Fired Calamari, served with scallions, Fresno peppers and a wasabi aioli dipping sauce, also returns as part of the year-round lineup. Rounding out the bar menu, Happy Hour introduces a sake category and a $12 Japanese whisky selection featuring Toki, Mars Iwai 45 and Nikka Coffey Grain, served on the rocks, neat or as a highball. “Happy Hour should be an opportunity to experience what our kitchen does best,” said Steve Solis, VP of Culinary at P.F. Chang’s. “With full-size appetizers and the new Sushi & Sip pairing, we’re putting the food front and center and giving guests a reason to make us part of their weekday plans.” Midweek, guests can also take advantage of Wine Wednesday, offering half-price bottles of wine, Champagne and sake all day at participating locations where permitted by applicable law for dine-in guests 21 and older. On the main menu, dishes that earned a following as limited-time offerings are now here to stay, including three premium entrées in a newly expanded Chef’s Favorites section: NY Prime Strip Steak Tataki: lightly seared steak with yuzu ponzu, butter, togarashi aioli and microgreens Lobster & Prawn Fried Rice: lobster and prawns tossed with P.F. articles.originalSummary: A Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) suspendeu nesta quarta-feira, 28, a venda da linguiça de carne suína defumada da marca KF Embutidos. Um laudo de análise microbiológica detectou a presença da bactéria Listeria monocytogenes no Lote 21/08/2026 do produto. Segundo a Anvisa, a Fábrica de Embutidos Zanetti informou que já iniciou o recolhimento voluntário do produto. A agência também suspendeu a fabricação, a distribuição, a propaganda e o consumo da linguiça. Em nota, a agência detalhou que o recolhimento voluntário é uma medida preventiva, adotada pela empresa interessada e demais empresas da cadeia produtiva de alimentos, que visa à imediata retirada de lotes de produtos do mercado de consumo. “Quando o alimento representa risco ou agravo à saúde do consumidor, o recolhimento é obrigatório”, reforçou a Anvisa. articles.title: INSS alerta para golpes que usam informação falsa sobre biometria
articles.titleKo: INSS alerta para golpes que usam informação falsa sobre biometria
articles.originalSummary: O Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social ( INSS ) divulgou nota para informar que são falsas informações que circulam na internet e nas redes sociais sobre o bloqueio de benefícios. Os conteúdos falsos dizem que seria necessário realizar um cadastro biométrico para impedir que o benefício fosse suspenso. No entanto, o INSS informa que essa exigência só é válida para novos pedidos feitos desde 21 de novembro de 2025. O órgão reforça que os beneficiários não precisam comparecer às agências do INSS para fazer cadastro biométrico. “Em realidade, nem sequer existe essa opção. Pois o registro biométrico significa que o cidadão precisa ter sua identidade confirmada por meio de uma biometria cadastrada em uma base oficial do governo”, diz a nota. Esse cadastramento é feito quando o cidadão emite algum documento público, como a Carteira de Identidade Nacional (CIN), a Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH) ou título de eleitor. Golpe O INSS alerta para tentativas de fraude que utilizam informações falsas sobre biometria para obter dados pessoais das vítimas. O órgão ressalta que não envia servidores à casa dos cidadãos para fazer a comprovação de vida, nem solicita senhas, dados bancários ou transferências de dinheiro. Também orienta para não clicar em links desconhecidos, uma vez que os golpistas usam páginas falsas para capturar dados e aplicá-los em outras fraudes. Isenção Mesmo entre quem solicitou o benefício após 21 de novembro do ano passado, nem todos precisam de documento com biometria. A legislação estabelece algumas exceções, como idosos com mais de 80 anos, migrantes, refugiados, apátridas, pessoas impossibilitadas de se deslocar por mais de 30 dias por motivo de saúde, entre outros. Além disso, também estão isentos da obrigatoriedade do registro biométrico os pedidos de salário-maternidade, benefícios por incapacidade e pensão por morte. Em caso de dúvida sobre a situação do benefício, o cidadão deve consultar o Meu INSS ou ligar para o 135. Com informações de Agência Brasil. Imagem: Marcello Casal Jr./Agência Brasil O post INSS alerta para golpes que usam informação falsa sobre biometria apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

articles.title: Heineken 0.0 leva ativações inspiradas na F1 a supermercados e lojas de conveniência
articles.titleKo: Heineken 0.0 leva ativações inspiradas na F1 a supermercados e lojas de conveniência
articles.originalSummary: A Heineken 0.0 leva ativações inspiradas na Fórmula 1 a supermercados, atacadistas e lojas de conveniência de São Paulo entre outubro e novembro. A campanha do Grupo Heineken inclui a House of F1, estrutura montada em duas lojas, ações promocionais de compre e ganhe, distribuição de brindes e degustações para aproximar a marca dos fãs do automobilismo no ponto de venda. Um dos destaques é a House of F1, instalada no Atacadão Interlagos e no Peg Pese Interlagos. Concebida como um mini museu temporário dedicado à Fórmula 1, a estrutura transforma ilhas de produtos em espaços de descoberta, com exposição de Heineken 0.0 e elementos visuais relacionados ao esporte. “A Fórmula 1 tem o poder de reunir pessoas em torno de uma paixão compartilhada, e queremos levar essa conexão também para o varejo. Com Heineken 0.0, ampliamos a presença da cerveja zero álcool em diferentes ocasiões, oferecendo ao shopper mais uma opção para acompanhar esses momentos. Nosso papel no Trade Marketing é traduzir essa conexão em experiências relevantes no ponto de venda”, explica Monah Feio, diretora nacional de Trade Marketing OFF-Premise do Grupo Heineken. A campanha também prevê materiais de visibilidade em diferentes formatos, como ilhas-pallet, pórticos, comunicações de gôndola, displays, adesivos de geladeira e sinalização nos caixas de autoatendimento. A estratégia busca ampliar a exposição da cerveja sem álcool ao longo da jornada de compra. Promoções e degustações Nos dias 6, 7 e 8 de novembro, das 10h às 18h, consumidores que comprarem a partir de R$ 30 em Heineken 0.0 nas lojas participantes do varejo poderão ganhar uma taça exclusiva de Fórmula 1. A ação abrange supermercados e atacadistas de redes como Assaí, Atacadão, Carrefour, Pão de Açúcar, Mambo, Peg Pese e Roldão, entre outros. Nas lojas de conveniência de postos de combustíveis, a mesma mecânica de compra mínima de R$ 30 dará acesso a brindes exclusivos de Fórmula 1, conforme a ação de cada estabelecimento. A programação inclui ainda decks ambientados e sampling em três lojas: AmPm, na Rua Ribeirão Claro, 91; BR Mania, na Rua General Furtado Nascimento, 599, e na Avenida Ibirapuera, 3.000. A degustação também ocorrerá em unidades da Select na Avenida do Jangadeiro, 34, e na Avenida Interlagos, 5.548. Com as ativações, o Grupo Heineken busca conectar a presença da Heineken 0.0 no varejo ao interesse do público pela Fórmula 1, combinando exposição de marca, experimentação e incentivo à compra. articles.title: Adidas transforma capivara em protagonista de linha de tênis
articles.titleKo: Adidas transforma capivara em protagonista de linha de tênis
articles.originalSummary: Associada à tranquilidade e à convivência, a capivara inspirou uma nova versão do Adidas Intimidation Low, silhueta lançada pela marca nos anos 1990. Desenvolvido em parceria com a Guadalupe, loja brasileira de referência na cultura sneaker, o modelo marca a primeira colaboração latino-americana da Adidas Consortium, plataforma dedicada a projetos com boutiques, designers e nomes do streetwear global. Nativa da América do Sul e presente em parques e áreas urbanas brasileiras, a capivara foi escolhida para representar o Brasil além dos clichês. A colaboração também explora o contraste entre o comportamento tranquilo do animal e o nome do tênis, Intimidation. “Escolhemos a capivara porque queríamos mostrar um Brasil menos óbvio, apostando em uma narrativa original e conectada à cultura local. É sempre emocionante saber que mais um tênis da Guadalupe vai rodar o mundo. Ser a primeira loja da América Latina a fazer um projeto com a Adidas Consortium é muito especial para a gente, para o Brasil e para todo mundo que nos acompanha desde o começo”, contou Pedro Prado, sócio da Guadalupe Store. Criada em 2005, a Adidas Consortium reúne algumas das colaborações mais exclusivas da marca e já desenvolveu projetos com referências internacionais do streetwear, como Sneakersnstuff, Overkill e Undefeated. Detalhes do modelo A Guadalupe reinterpretou o Intimidation Low, modelo que combina referências esportivas e urbanas. A edição limitada traz predominância de tons marrons e mantém elementos da construção original, como a entressola esculpida e o solado Feet You Wear, inspirado nas formas naturais do pé. O cabedal combina mesh e nobuck sintético. A parceria também inclui a versão Adidas Intimidation Low x Guadalupe “Albino”, desenvolvida em branco. A edição não será comercializada e terá distribuição restrita a amigos, parceiros e pessoas diretamente ligadas à colaboração. O nome faz referência à raridade da capivara albina e à quantidade limitada de pares produzidos. “É uma grande honra ter uma colaboração brasileira integrando a adidas Consortium. Uma plataforma tão exclusiva, que celebra criatividade e autenticidade, merecia um projeto desenvolvido com o nível de excelência construído ao lado da Guadalupe. O adidas Intimidation Low x Guadalupe representa um marco para o mercado de lifestyle na América Latina, unindo design inovador e um conceito profundamente conectado à nossa cultura e identidade”, afirma Bárbara Ikari, gerente sênior de Comunicação da Adidas no Brasil. O Adidas Intimidation Low x Guadalupe chega ao mercado em 5 de novembro, por R$ 1.199,99, no site e nas lojas da Guadalupe nos bairros do Paraíso e Bom Retiro, em São Paulo. O lançamento também estará disponível em países como Inglaterra, Grécia, Japão, Coreia do Sul, África do Sul e Alemanha. articles.title: The Old China Hand in Clerkenwell sold to Southampton Arms operator
articles.titleKo: The Old China Hand in Clerkenwell sold to Southampton Arms operator
articles.originalSummary: Pete Holt, the pub operator behind the Southampton Arms in Kentish Town, has bought The Old China Hand, a Grade II listed pub in Clerkenwell, London. Located at 8 Tysoe Street, a short distance from Exmouth Market, the property has been owned and operated by Mike Peck and Rowena Smith for approximately 20 years. The sale marks the end of their two-decade tenure as they retire. Dating from around 1856, The Old China Hand occupies a three-storey building that retains much of its period character.

articles.title: Homegrown Tap & Dough Opens First Colorado Springs Restaurant
articles.titleKo: Homegrown Tap & Dough Opens First Colorado Springs Restaurant
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Homegrown Tap & Dough opened its first Colorado Springs restaurant on Tuesday, October 27, at 5710 S. Carefree Circle, near North Powers Boulevard and South Carefree Circle. The opening marks the seventh Homegrown location and the first Colorado Springs restaurant for Denver-based Gastamo Group. The 6,000-square-foot restaurant seats 215 guests inside and 106 on the patio. The opening created 104 jobs, and the restaurant is run by Kelley Compton, Gastamo Group’s first managing partner. The menu features Homegrown’s signature hand-tossed pizzas, pasta dishes, and shareable starters, with gluten-free and vegetarian options, Colorado craft beer, and handcrafted cocktails. Happy hour runs Sunday through Thursday from 2–6 p.m. and, for the first time at Homegrown, again from 8 p.m. to close. Available at the bar and on the patio, specials include select 22-ounce draft beers, wines, and cocktails for $6, plus bites starting at $6. “We’ve been working on our first Colorado Springs restaurant for three years, and we’re stoked it’s finally here,” said Peter Newlin, CEO of Gastamo Group. “We love this community and wanted to show up as a real neighbor, not just another new restaurant. Partnering with Mt. Carmel in our first full month is how we give back to the people who make Colorado Springs what it is.” Throughout November, the restaurant will donate $1 for every 14-inch pizza sold to Mt. Carmel Veterans Service Center. The organization supports veterans, active-duty service members, and their families across Southern Colorado through transition and employment assistance, behavioral health and wellness programs, and connections to community resources. Active-duty service members and veterans also receive 10 percent off every visit at all Gastamo Group restaurants. “Supporting our veterans, military members, and their families takes a community, and we’re grateful to Homegrown Tap & Dough for turning a delicious meal into an opportunity to give back,” said Bob McLaughlin, executive director of Mt. Carmel Veterans Service Center. “This partnership will help us connect those who have served with the support they need. Together, we’re honoring their service through action and helping ensure no veteran falls through the cracks.” The opening follows a complete redevelopment of the property. The team gutted the original building, expanded the patio, and added exterior structures, collaborating with architecture firm HSU Office on architecture and art. Newlin described the project as one of the most ambitious builds in Gastamo Group’s history. The dining room pays tribute to the region’s military history through a large American flag installation by Colorado-based artist Dolan Geiman. The piece incorporates authentic military memorabilia donated by families locally and across the country, including handwritten letters exchanged between overseas servicemen and their families during World War II and the Korean War. A U.S. Navy garrison cap donated by a retired naval officer sits in the lower corner of the flag’s blue field. Marine Corps insignia, Naval Reserve patches, wartime songbooks, and vintage Colorado keepsakes complete the installation. A Ski Patrol gondola and vintage Tenth Mountain Division skis honor the World War II Army division that trained in Colorado’s high country. Homegrown Tap & Dough is open Sunday through Thursday from 11 a.m.–9 p.m. and Friday and Saturday from 11 a.m.–10 p.m. More information is available at tapanddough.com. articles.title: SHŌ Introduces Eight-Drink Zero-Proof Pairing for Plant-Based Omakase
articles.titleKo: SHŌ Introduces Eight-Drink Zero-Proof Pairing for Plant-Based Omakase
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . SHŌ is expanding the language of pairing with an eight-drink experience created expressly for Shōjin, the restaurant’s new plant-based omakase. Developed by Bar Director Pepe Pereyra, the pairing combines the ritual and structure of classic wine service with the inventiveness of modern cocktail-making, unfolding as a zero-proof progression that evolves in step with Executive Chef Mari Katsumura’s vegan tasting menu. Rather than assemble a traditional lineup of juice-forward mocktails, Pereyra set out to recreate the way wine behaves alongside food, including how its acidity, aromatics, and texture unfold across the palate and how its finish carries into the next bite. At the foundation is a selection of nonalcoholic wines from Oddbird, each traditionally vinified before the alcohol is gently removed through vacuum distillation to preserve its character. Working with expressions including a Grenache-Syrah-Mourvèdre blend, sparkling rosé, sparkling orange wine, and a Riesling-Sylvaner white blend, Pereyra layers in teas, organic shrubs, and ingredients drawn directly from the kitchen—from red miso syrup and strawberry vinegar to verjus and fresh citrus—giving each pour its own identity. “Just as working without traditional proteins opened new creative possibilities for Chef Mari, working without alcohol pushed me to think differently about every glass,” says Pereyra. “We both let the ingredients guide us, and for me that meant chasing the way wine moves with food, rather than simply replacing it.” Served off ice in wine glasses, the drinks are designed to be swirled, sipped, and experienced alongside each course. The progression opens bright and effervescent, pairing the canapés with an alcohol-removed Grenache-Syrah-Mourvèdre blend layered with Mallorca melon, watermelon, and saline. As the menu unfolds, the drinks move into more savory, umami-rich territory. The hot somen, for example, is accompanied by a Tempranillo-based pour accented with red cabbage shrub and yuzu. The complete spirit-free pairing journey includes the following. Grenache-Syrah-Mourvèdre, Mallorca Melon, Watermelon, and Saline Paired with the opening canapés. Seedlip Spice 94, Red Verjus, Pineapple, Beet, and Red Miso Paired with the beet crudo. Pinot Blanc-Riesling, Wölffer Verjus, Orange, Watermelon, and Lapsang Souchong Paired with the sweet corn velouté. Pinot Blanc-Riesling, Cucumber, Yuzu, and Celery Shrub Paired with the tofu, artichoke, and broccolini hand rolls. Sparkling Rosé, Seedlip Spice 94, and Umami Shrub Made with yuzu, wild kombu, ginger, and sake lees vinegar; paired with the eggplant and mushroom hand rolls. French White Blend, Wölffer Verjus, Ginger, Yuzu, and Sesame Oil Paired with the pea soufflé. Tempranillo, Red Verjus, Red Cabbage Shrub, and Yuzu Paired with the hot somen. Seedlip Spice 94, Red Verjus, Umami Shrub, Strawberry Vinegar, and Red Miso Paired with the hojicha, almond, and chocolate soft serve. A Broader Beverage Landscape The Shōjin pairing is part of a broader beverage program led by General Manager and Sommelier Preston Smith, who develops distinct wine, sake, and platinum pairings around SHŌ’s evolving menus. Each progression is built course by course. Sake selections span different prefectures, brewing methods, and yeast strains, while the wine pairings move across regions, colors, and styles to complement the restaurant’s Japanese foundation and global influences. The platinum pairing, a guest favorite, brings together standout wine, sake, and spirit selections in one highly curated progression. “Pairings should never feel like checking a box or following a formula,” says Smith. “We want each pour to create a genuine connection with the course while introducing guests to producers, regions and styles they may not have encountered before. articles.title: The Cheesecake Factory’s Traffic Surges as Social Buzz Brings New Guests
articles.titleKo: The Cheesecake Factory’s Traffic Surges as Social Buzz Brings New Guests
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Cheesecake Factory's same-store sales rose 15.2 percent in Q3. The Cheesecake Factory’s Q3 traffic surge is giving the casual chain a chance to turn social media attention into lasting guest loyalty, and it is investing in the restaurant experience to make those visits count. During the quarter, same-store sales climbed 15.2 percent, driven by 9.5 percent traffic growth that outperformed the Black Box casual-dining index by 940 basis points. Annualized average unit volumes exceeded $13.9 million, setting another record during what president David Gordon described as typically the company’s slowest quarter. The gains stretched across regions, meal periods, and days of the week. Off-premises business held steady at approximately 21 percent of sales. The company’s challenge now is converting that demand into repeat business without sacrificing the service that brought guests through the doors. “Certainly, we’ll continue to monitor those social channels, influence them appropriately when we think we should and, most importantly, as I said earlier, execute against those new sales and the traffic growth because we don’t want it to be a one-and-done situation,” Gordon said during the Q3 earnings call. “It never has been at Cheesecake Factory. We’re building brand loyalty and guest loyalty for the long term.” READ MORE : Cheesecake Factory and Flower Child Continue to Compete with ‘Everybody and Nobody’ The Cheesecake Factory’s Sales Flywheel is Picking Up Speed The Cheesecake Factory Hits Record Sales and Exceeds Expectations in First Quarter Social media discovery has helped introduce younger consumers to the brand. CFO Matthew Clark said a large percentage of incoming guests skew younger, although four months of momentum did not provide enough information to assess their long-term visit frequency. However, it’s important to note, sales trends have been consistent through that four-month period, and that’s without significant swings tied to the timing of organic social content. One beneficiary was Cajun Salmon, an existing menu item that attracted attention through viral customization ideas. Guests who came to try it also brought dining companions who ordered established favorites, including Chicken Madeira and Avocado Eggrolls. The chain recorded 3.3 percent positive sales mix alongside 2.4 percent pricing. Cajun Salmon contributed because it sits toward the upper end of the entrée menu, but Clark also pointed to an increase in alcohol incidence. Cheesecake incidence was flat at an all-time high. Menu development will continue on its established schedule of two changes annually. The recent success does not signal a faster rollout of new products. “The cadence is the two menu changes a year, and that will be the same cadence moving into next year and for the foreseeable future,” Gordon said. “I wouldn’t anticipate that’s going to change.” The company is also building a more direct connection with guests through Cheesecake Rewards and its app, which launched in the second quarter. Gordon said personalized offers are helping support repeat visits, and the app is taking on a larger role in digital ordering and guest communication. Weekly rewards member acquisition continues to run at twice the level recorded before the app’s launch. Clark said rewards participants visit more frequently, giving the company another way to sustain sales after the initial wave of social discovery. Cheesecake Factory’s performance lifted companywide revenue above $1.033 billion, its second consecutive quarterly record. Adjusted EBITDA rose 38 percent to $98.7 million. At the flagship concept, restaurant-level profit margin expanded 240 basis points to 18.7 percent. Labor costs declined 80 basis points as a percentage of companywide sales, helped by sales leverage. articles.title: TipHaus Helps Upward Projects Simplify Tip Calculations Across Multiple Brands
articles.titleKo: TipHaus Helps Upward Projects Simplify Tip Calculations Across Multiple Brands
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . As Upward Projects continues to grow its collection of concepts, its partnership with TipHaus supports accurate, consistent, and efficient tip management across the group. Upward Projects, the Phoenix-based hospitality group behind Postino, Windsor, Churn, Federal Pizza, and Joyride Taco House, has partnered with TipHaus to automate tip management and give its teams faster, more transparent access to their tip earnings across its 40-plus restaurants. For a multi-concept group running distinct brands across multiple states, tip management had long meant manual, time-consuming tip reconciliation, with each concept carrying its own rules and pay structures. Since adopting TipHaus in the fall of 2025, Upward Projects has replaced that manual work with a single automated system that calculates and distributes tips through the tools the group already runs, Toast and Crunchtime, and gives hourly team members next-day tip access to their earnings through Earned Tip Access®. “At Upward Projects, our people are at the heart of everything we do, so giving our teams faster, more transparent access to their tips was an easy call. Before TipHaus, reconciling and distributing tips took our team members and managers about 2 hours per day; with TipHaus it takes a fraction of that time, saving us roughly 30 hours a month per location. With Earned Tip Access and digital payouts, our hourly employees can also access their earnings the next day, giving our teams a more modern pay experience while lifting significant administrative weight off our managers,” said Brian Anderson, Vice President of Technology at Upward Projects. “The app also gives our team members greater visibility into their earnings, which saves our managers time running and explaining reports, and the payroll export merges seamlessly with our payroll provider, making it easy for our team to verify and confirm earned tips,” Anderson added. TipHaus integrates directly with Toast and Crunchtime, pulling sales, shift, and labor data automatically so that tip calculations run without manual data entry at each location. Rather than forcing a rigid, one-size-fits-all model, TipHaus configures to the specific rules of each concept, allowing Upward Projects to standardize oversight across the group while honoring how each brand operates. Through Earned Tip Access, employees can reach their earned tips the next day, giving teams a modern, transparent pay experience. “My wife and I are regulars at Postino for weekend brunch, so we have seen firsthand how much care Upward Projects puts into its guests and its teams. Behind the scenes, they run several distinct concepts, each with its own systems and tip structures, and we specialize in shaping TipHaus around what each one needs instead of asking them to work within our platform’s limits. By automating that complexity across the group and integrating with the Toast and Crunchtime systems they already use, we help Upward Projects deliver consistent, accurate payouts and give their teams faster, more transparent access to their earnings. It is a privilege to support a group whose restaurants we love,” said Kirk Grogan, COO and Co-Founder of TipHaus. As Upward Projects continues to grow its collection of concepts, its partnership with TipHaus supports accurate, consistent, and efficient tip management across the group, freeing managers to focus on hospitality and giving team members a faster, more modern pay experience. articles.title: Jack Brown’s Beer & Burger Joint Bought by Green Shoot Brands
articles.titleKo: Jack Brown’s Beer & Burger Joint Bought by Green Shoot Brands
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Jack Brown's Beer & Burger Joint was founded in 2009. Jack Brown’s Beer & Burger Joint has been acquired by Florida-based Green Shoot Brands, according to several media reports. The 22-unit casual-dining chain operates across seven states. Financial terms were not disclosed, according to the Nashville Business Journal . Founders Aaron Ludwig and Mike Sabin and president Jason Owenby will continue running the company. A Green Shoot spokesperson told The Tennessean the acquisition includes all Jack Brown’s locations, with further expansion planned. “The burger, the beer and the feel won’t change,” the spokesperson told The Tennessean. Ludwig and Sabin opened the first Jack Brown’s in Harrisonburg, Virginia, in 2009. The childhood friends built the concept around burgers, craft beer, and a dive-bar atmosphere, eventually expanding into Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Tennessee. The menu centers on American Wagyu beef burgers with toppings that range from macaroni and cheese to peanut butter. The Greg Brady features housemade macaroni and cheese, American cheese, and barbecue potato chips, while the Elvis combines peanut butter, applewood-smoked bacon, American cheese, and Duke’s mayonnaise. Fries and deep-fried Oreos round out the streamlined food lineup. Craft beer is another cornerstone. Jack Brown’s stocks local and international selections and operates the Notch Club, which offers merchandise and beer-tasting trips for participating guests. The acquisition adds a burger-and-beer concept to Green Shoot’s nine-brand portfolio. The company operates 410 units across 27 states and Washington, D.C., with more than $500 million in system sales, according to its website. The group franchises with Auntie Anne’s, Cinnabon, Jamba, Carvel, Nothing Bundt Cakes, Little Caesars, PopUp Bagels, and Dave’s Hot Chicken. Green Shoot began in 2019 with the acquisition of Fresh Dining Concepts. It expanded through acquisitions within its original snack-brand portfolio before broadening its restaurant holdings under CEO Mike Evans, who joined in 2024. Nothing Bundt Cakes and Little Caesars followed in 2025, with PopUp Bagels, Dave’s, and Jack Brown’s added this year. The ownership change also includes the departure of an early Jack Brown’s investor. Chenault Sanders told the Nashville Business Journal he sold his interests in the restaurant business to support its continued growth in Nashville. Sanders and his partners will retain the real estate housing the Germantown and Clarksville restaurants. articles.title: Lucille’s Smokehouse Bar-B-Que Launches Black Gold Sauce and Two New Entrees
articles.titleKo: Lucille’s Smokehouse Bar-B-Que Launches Black Gold Sauce and Two New Entrees
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Lucille’s Smokehouse Bar-B-Que has built a reputation on the hallmark of great Southern-inspired bar-b-que. Lucille’s Smokehouse Bar-B-Que, the award-winning destination for authentic Southern bar-b-que that has welcomed guests with slow-smoked meats and down-home hospitality since 1999, announced the November 5 launch of Black Gold, its first new signature bar-b-que sauce in over five years. Building on 25 years of bar-b-que craftsmanship, Black Gold brings black garlic, slow-aged until dark and sweet as molasses, to two brand-new, celebratory entrees: Black Garlic BBQ Baby Back Ribs: Lucille’s signature tender, slow-smoked baby back ribs brushed and glazed with rich, dark Black Gold BBQ sauce. BBQ Tri Tip with Black Garlic Butter: Tender, certified Angus Beef tri tip smoked to perfection and crowned with a decadent Black Garlic Butter Sauce. Also launching on November 5 is a new Pumpkin Top Cocktail with Ketel One Vodka, Owen’s Espresso Martini Mix, and vanilla syrup served on the rocks with housemade pumpkin cold foam. Both are coming to the menu just in time for the holiday gathering season and will be available at all 19 Lucille’s locations across California, Nevada and Arizona. Lucille’s has built a reputation on the hallmark of great Southern-inspired bar-b-que: expertly seasoned meats, patient, low-and-slow smoking, scratch made favorites, and genuine Southern hospitality. That dedication has the earned the brand repeat reader-voted honors for its Southern specialties over the years. Black Gold marks the latest step in Lucille’s evolution, introducing a distinctive new flavor while honoring the smoky richness and comforting, soulful food that define the brand. “Black garlic is having a moment, and we saw an opportunity to bring this bold flavor to the comforting bar-b-que our guests know and love,” said Joan Hansen, vice president of marketing for Lucille’s Smokehouse Bar-B-Que. “Black Gold is a meaningful addition to our sauce lineup, balancing deep savory notes with a natural sweetness that pairs beautifully with our slow-smoked meats. We’re excited to introduce this new flavor and give our guests something special to enjoy as we head into the holiday season.” For more information or to find your nearest Lucille’s location, visit www.lucillesbbq.com. articles.title: Two Red Robin Directors Exit as Investment Goals Are Substantially Achieved
articles.titleKo: Two Red Robin Directors Exit as Investment Goals Are Substantially Achieved
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Red Robin Gourmet Burgers, Inc., a casual dining restaurant chain serving an innovative selection of high-quality gourmet burgers in a family-friendly atmosphere, together with JCP Investment Management, LLC (“JCP”) and Jumana Capital (“Jumana”), announced that James Pappas, Managing Member of JCP, and Chris Martin, Managing Director of Jumana, resigned from the Board of Directors of Red Robin, effective October 23, 2026. Pappas and Martin joined the Board in December 2024 in connection with an additional investment in Red Robin by Jumana and JCP. The strategic objectives behind that investment have now been substantially achieved. In connection with the resignations, the Board will decrease to six directors, five of whom will be independent. Since December 2024, Red Robin has meaningfully strengthened its operating and financial position under its First Choice Plan. The Company has refreshed its menu, deepened its leadership team, improved restaurant-level margins, and advanced its refranchising program by selling more than 100 Company-operated restaurants. Earlier this month, these efforts enabled the Company to refinance its prior credit agreement with a new five-year, $115 million senior secured commercial bank credit facility led by JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. The new facility, consisting of a $90 million term loan and a $25 million revolving credit facility, carries meaningfully lower borrowing costs than the prior agreement and gives management greater flexibility to continue executing its First Choice Plan. “When we invested in Red Robin, we saw an iconic brand with a clear opportunity to improve operations and strengthen the balance sheet,” said James Pappas and Chris Martin. “Dave Pace and his team have executed on that opportunity. The operational improvements and refranchising program culminated in a lower-cost commercial bank refinancing, which positions management to focus on growing the business rather than managing leverage.” “On behalf of our management team and our Board, I want to express our appreciation for James and Chris and their contributions and collaboration in the boardroom and their unwavering confidence in the management team as we navigated a highly complex path to firming up our balance sheet and our financial foundation,” said Dave Pace, CEO and president of Red Robin. Pappas and Martin continued, “This is the right time for us to step off the Board. We have great confidence in the leadership team and our fellow directors, and we believe Red Robin is well positioned to build on its momentum.” Additional information can be found in the Company’s Form 8-K filed today with the Securities and Exchange Commission. articles.title: Southeast Portland’s 82 Acres Features Farm-Grown Ingredients on Fall Menu
articles.titleKo: Southeast Portland’s 82 Acres Features Farm-Grown Ingredients on Fall Menu
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . 82 Acres in Southeast Portland is featuring a fall menu developed by chef Will Preisch in collaboration with the team at Abbey Road Farm in Carlton. The restaurant, which comes from the farm’s owners and Preisch, a veteran of Le Pigeon and Holdfast, plans seasonal menus beginning with seed meetings before crops are planted. Fall dishes include Delicata Squash Katsu, stuffed with farm-raised lamb sausage, fried katsu-style, and served with house-made bulldog sauce, stewed farm cherries, apples, carrots, and an egg jam made from farm yolks. The Squash Carpaccio features thinly shaved honeynut and red kuri squash that is frozen and thawed to develop its texture. It is dressed with curry leaf oil and a farm-raisin and caper chutney, then finished with roasted leeks, white beans cooked in Parmesan stock, sesame, and urfa biber, a Turkish chili pepper. The Farm Salad draws inspiration from a Lyonnaise salad, with farm-sourced tesa, egg, herbs, and smoked egg yolk. Tomato Toast combines blistered farm tomatoes with cheddar mornay, prepared Welsh rarebit-style, and Szechuan and mustard oil over a vegan tomato XO made with dehydrated heirloom tomatoes, fennel, smoked tofu, star anise, cognac, and dark soy glaze. The Carrot Salad includes farm carrots over a purée of carrots, onions, and bacon cooked in chicken fat and glazed in red wine. The dish is topped with Belper Knolle cheese and smoked pecans, dressed with a shallot and harra spice vinaigrette, and finished with radicchio. Dessert includes a s’mores ice cream sandwich made with toasted marshmallow semifreddo, graham crackers, and a black sesame shell. Located at 2032 SE Clinton St., 82 Acres serves dinner Wednesday through Sunday from 5 p.m. to close. A full bar offers specialty cocktails, beer and wine, and catering is available for group gatherings and events offsite. Founded in Mobile, Alabama, in 2010, Rock N Roll Sushi has grown from a Gulf Coast original into a national concept with more than 80 locations. articles.title: Consumo em supermercados cresce 6,5% após proibição das bets, aponta Abras
articles.titleKo: Consumo em supermercados cresce 6,5% após proibição das bets, aponta Abras
articles.originalSummary: O consumo em supermercados cresceu 6,5% no Brasil na semana de 5 a 11 de outubro, em comparação com o mesmo período de 2025. O avanço ocorre após a publicação da Medida Provisória 1.394/2026 , em 25 de setembro, que proibiu as bets no País, segundo estudos da Associação Brasileira de Supermercados ( Abras ). O crescimento foi mais expressivo nas regiões Sul e na área que compreende Minas Gerais, Espírito Santo e interior do Rio de Janeiro, ambas com alta de 10,6%. O Nordeste registrou avanço de 6,5%, seguido pelo interior de São Paulo, com 5,6%. Na Grande Rio de Janeiro, o crescimento foi de 4%; no Centro-Oeste, de 3,6%; e na Grande São Paulo, de 1,2%. Na semana seguinte, de 12 a 18 de outubro, o consumo no varejo alimentar brasileiro avançou 6,3% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. O Sul permaneceu na liderança regional, com alta de 9%, seguido pela área que compreende Minas Gerais, Espírito Santo e interior do Rio de Janeiro, com 7,1%, e pela Grande Rio de Janeiro, com 6%. O interior de São Paulo registrou crescimento de 5,6%, enquanto a Grande São Paulo avançou 5,5%. Nordeste e Centro-Oeste tiveram altas de 4,5% e 3,5%, respectivamente. Produtos essenciais impulsionam consumo Segundo a Abras, o crescimento foi observado especialmente na cesta de produtos essenciais, que inclui arroz, óleo, macarrão e café. A tendência abrange supermercados, atacarejos, mercearias e outros formatos do varejo alimentar. A associação também relaciona o movimento a dados públicos do Banco Central, que apontariam uma redução de 10% no número de transações via Pix no País após a proibição das bets. Atualmente, a queda seria de 7%. Os dados indicam uma coincidência temporal entre a mudança nas transações via Pix e o aumento do consumo no varejo alimentar. No entanto, essa relação, por si só, não comprova que a proibição das apostas tenha causado o crescimento nas compras dos supermercados. articles.title: Aliado de Trump diz que Flávio Bolsonaro chegou aos EUA
articles.titleKo: Aliado de Trump diz que Flávio Bolsonaro chegou aos EUA
articles.originalSummary: O investidor e ex-secretário de Turismo do México, Simón Levy, publicou uma postagem nas redes sociais nesta terça-feira, 27, relatando que Flávio Bolsonaro teria chegado aos Estados Unidos (EUA), em uma articulação liderada pelo secretário de Estado norte-americano, Marco Rubio. A possível fuga de Flávio, menos de 48 horas após perder as eleições presidenciais, também foi confirmada pela agência de notícias Reuters. Nenhuma autoridade oficial do Brasil ou dos EUA, entretanto, confirma saída de Flávio do País. “Como relatei há algumas horas, Flávio Bolsonaro chegou em segurança aos Estados Unidos. O cérebro por trás dessa operação é o Secretário de Estado dos EUA Marco Rubio. Dos Estados Unidos, livre e seguro, Flávio liderará a oposição contra Lula”, escreveu. A postagem foi feita por volta das 15h30. Em outra publicação, menos de 30 minutos depois, Levy acrescentou que essa fuga recebeu o nome de Operação Alba. Levy é empresário e advogado e se autodescreve publicamente como um aliado próximo e alguém que serve a Donald Trump e ao movimento MAGA [Make America Great Again, no inglês]. Post de Simón Levy sobre fuga de Flávio Bolsonaro aos Estados Unidos. Foto: SimonLevyMx/X – SimonLevyMx/X A Agência Brasil procurou a assessoria de Flávio, mas não recebeu retorno. O senador não chegou a entregar seus passaportes à Polícia Federal (PF) após decisão do ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF). A decisão está em segredo de justiça e foi tornada pública pelo senador em suas redes sociais. A ordem judicial faz parte do processo em que Flávio e o advogado Willer Tomaz são investigados no STF por lavagem de dinheiro. Por causa do descumprimento, os passaportes do parlamentar foram cancelados diretamente pela PF. Com informações de Agência Brasil.
